claims.text: PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts can catalyze complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation.
The baseline PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has high activity and selectivity for 12-electron ethanol oxidation.
High selectivity for complete ethanol oxidation is governed by synergy arising from a random, atomically mixed distribution of the six metals.
Atomic mixing in PtPdRhRuIrOs creates isolated Pt and Pd active sites.
Neighboring Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os atoms electronically modify Pt and Pd sites through ligand effects.
The neighboring elements shift the d-band centers of Pt and Pd sites.
The electronic modification optimizes adsorption and desorption energies for ethanol and its reaction intermediates.
Optimized adsorption and desorption at modified Pt/Pd sites facilitates the complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation pathway.
The as-synthesized catalyst is rapidly quenched and has a random, atomically uniform distribution of all six metals.
Controlled thermal annealing can induce partial ordering or elemental clustering in PtPdRhRuIrOs without changing its overall composition.
Annealing reduces the isolation of Pt and Pd sites and increases their clustering.
Ordering or clustering diminishes the ligand synergy present in the random solid solution.
The loss of ligand synergy changes intermediate adsorption energies and favors incomplete, approximately 4-electron ethanol oxidation.
Relative to the as-synthesized baseline, the annealed catalyst will have a lower proportion of complete 12-electron oxidation products.
The predicted effect is scoped to tests with matched applied potential, temperature, electrolyte pH, electrochemical configuration, and mass-transport conditions.
The magnitude of the selectivity decrease is uncertain.
If confirmed ordering or clustering produces the same or improved 12-electron selectivity relative to the random baseline, the proposed causal role of random mixing is falsified.
